  • Strong full-stack engineering experience, including modern frontend frameworks, backend services, API development, and integration with databases and external systems.
  • Hands-on experience designing, deploying, and maintaining applications using modern cloud infrastructure, including cloud-native architecture, deployment automation, and production operations.
  • Proficiency with modern frontend and backend programming languages, with the ability to quickly learn and contribute to new technologies.

  • Familiarity with AI-assisted software development tools and the ability to use them effectively while critically evaluating generated code for accuracy, security, and maintainability.
  • Strong problem-solving and communication skills, with experience collaborating across engineering, product, and other business functions.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

**We are interested in every qualified candidate who is eligible to work in the United States. However, we are not able to sponsor or transfer visas at this time.

Although not required, we’d love to see roots in:

  • Production experience with Python and TypeScript, ideally including frameworks such as FastAPI, React, or similar technologies.
  • Experience developing geospatial or data-intensive applications, including GIS, spatial databases such as PostGIS, mapping technologies, or large-scale scientific data pipelines.
  • Experience integrating AI/ML capabilities, large language models, or agentic workflows into production software applications.

Overview

We are looking for a skilled Platform Software Engineer to design and build the shared components, integration frameworks, and tooling that empower engineering teams across the organization. The ideal candidate brings hands-on experience with healthcare data standards, workflow automation, and full-stack web development. You will work at the intersection of backend services, cloud infrastructure, and healthcare interoperability—building the foundational layers that accelerate development velocity and consistency across multiple domains.

Key Responsibilities

  • Platform Development: Design, implement, and maintain reusable platform components, libraries, and SDKs that enable engineering teams to build automation and integration solutions efficiently and consistently.
  • Healthcare Integration: Develop and maintain integrations using industry-standard healthcare protocols and formats including EDI (X12), HL7 (v2/v3), FHIR (R4), and RESTful APIs connecting EHRs, payers, clearinghouses, and third-party systems.

  • CI/CD & DevOps: Operate comfortably within CI/CD pipelines using Azure DevOps or GitHub Actions; contribute to infrastructure managed via IaC tools such as Terraform, Bicep, or ARM templates.
  • Compliance & Security: Ensure all platform components adhere to healthcare data privacy and security requirements (HIPAA), and follow Azure security best practices including RBAC, Key Vault, and Entra ID.
  • Documentation: Produce clear, thorough technical documentation for platform components, APIs, integration patterns, and developer usage guides.
  • Collaboration: Partner with cross-functional teams to understand integration needs, define platform standards, and provide technical guidance on platform adoption.

Preferred Qualifications

data.description:
About GiveDirectly

What if the most effective way to fight poverty was also the simplest: give people money and trust them to decide what they need?

Since 2011, GiveDirectly has proven that idea at scale. We’ve delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty and crisis across 15 countries, and rigorous research shows the results: healthier kids, stronger businesses, sturdier homes, and more resilient families and local economies. Cash is now widely recognized as one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid.

Our ambition goes beyond our own programs. We want cash to become the benchmark for aid, much as the index fund became the benchmark for investing, so that every aid dollar is held to one question: is this doing more good than giving the money directly to people living in poverty?

We’re growing fast, and this is a rare and important moment to join.

We expect to hit $1B in revenue in 2026 with significant growth forecast for 2027. At the same time we are building a new technology stack and operating model designed for a roughly 10x change in scale, and we are actively pursuing partnerships with major funders to move even more money in bigger ways, to people who need it. We are known for our extensive integration of technology into field processes; our quantitative approach to performance measurement; and our commitment to rigorous, independent, experimental evaluation of our impact, with multiple Randomized Control Trials completed and others in progress.

How we work

Our team spans 20+ countries and 69 languages. Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical. We expect high ownership and give people real responsibility early. Our values are central to how we hire, work, and grow, and they are deliberately opinionated:

  1. Recipients first. Recipients’ preferences come before those of donors or ourselves.
  2. Team next. We optimize for organizational success, not individual success.
  3. Be proactively candid. We say what we believe and share information openly.
  4. Create positive energy. We aim to be a source of energy for colleagues, not a drain.
  5. Think rigorously; act quickly. We reason from first principles, then act rather than debate.
  6. Know yourself and grow. We own our imperfections and seek feedback to grow.
  7. Accept reality. Propose solutions. We focus on what can change and bring solutions, not just problems.
  8. Be productively ambitious. We take risks for step-change impact, not incremental progress.

If they describe how you like to work and they energize you, this could be a great fit.

Want to learn more? Read and listen:

We are one of Time100’s Most Influential Companies of 2026, and our work has been covered by The Economist, NPR, TED, and The Washington Post. We're now preparing to deliver billions of dollars a year to people in extreme poverty, if funding allows. Read our CEO's essay on what that will take.

About this role:

Are you an experienced engineer at the stage of your career where, above all, you want to do good?

This role is about using engineering to support fundraising: delighting our donors; helping our fundraisers; getting donations recorded and safely started on their journey to our recipients; telling donors and the public about what happens to their gifts. A bit of website development. A lot of plumbing.

The good news about this position:

  • You will make a difference to people in extreme poverty
  • You will work independently, with few constraints
  • You will work directly with lovely people from across our fundraising teams

The trade-offs:

  1. There is only one other fundraising engineer and mostly you will be working on your own
  2. Our technology is a mixture of boring (Laravel, PHP, plain JS, HTML and CSS) and legacy (Salesforce, Wordpress, wrangling CSV files sent by our partners)
  3. We're growing, but this is a role for someone who values depth and impact over a fast title ladder.

The maybe good maybe bad news about the role depending on who you are:

  • We are all in on AI where it allows us to get more $ to people in extreme poverty

If you want a role where you will be part of a bigger engineering team, working in Python or working on more complex tasks, then please take a look at our other engineering roles.

This role is right for you if:

  • You care about our mission
  • You agree with our values
  • You have the right to work in one of the countries we're able to hire from (you can check the current list here).
  • You're happy working remotely, and taking meetings across East Africa Time and US Eastern Time.
  • You are happy to travel to meet your colleagues in the US, Europe and Africa a few weeks a year
  • You are fluent in English
  • You have 4+ years of engineering experience
  • You're happy working autonomously: defining what needs doing, doing it, getting it tested and launched, fixing the bugs, and hustling to make progress every day.
  • You're comfortable being on-call on peak donation days (Giving Tuesday and the last weeks of the year), including owning an incident: working out what matters, communicating with fundraisers, and debugging on legacy and others' code, sometimes when no other engineers are available.
  • You are happy with our boring and legacy technologies (Laravel, PHP, plain JS, HTML, CSS, Salesforce, Wordpress, SQL, wrangling csv files etc). You don’t have to be experienced in all of them, but you do have to be genuinely happy to use them (many engineers are not…).
  • You are happy and skilled at working directly with non-engineers on messy, poorly defined, rapidly changing, sometimes boring tasks

Compensation

At GiveDirectly, we strive to pay our employees generously and equitably. We use an accredited third party salary aggregator to calculate what we believe to be competitive pay based on role, location, and cost of living. We also have a no negotiation policy to ensure we are paying staff equitably across roles. Read more about our compensation philosophy here.

Unless otherwise noted, the benefits stipend may be used to cover benefits or taken as additional taxable income.

United States

This role is fully remote, so if you are not based in the US, UK or Kenya, we will share an estimated salary benchmark for the country you are based in during the hiring process.

Why work at GiveDirectly?

At GiveDirectly, we work to ensure that you have everything you need to excel in your role and on your team, including:

About The Job

Navan is an all-in-one travel, corporate card, and expense management solution that eliminates the hassles of corporate travel & expense management while giving finance leaders real-time spend visibility and control.

The Frontend Architect plays a pivotal role in shaping the future of Navan's frontend infrastructure and developer experience across the organization. This role is central to architecting and maintaining the frontend platform that enables 20+ engineering teams to deploy independently while maintaining high quality standards. The Frontend Architect is essential to our mission, building shared libraries, developer tooling, and infrastructure, evolving the platform for both human and AI-assisted development, and driving performance and reliability initiatives.

What You'll Do

  • Architect Micro-Frontend Infrastructure: Design and evolve micro-frontend platform using Module Federation in React & Angular. Create and maintain shared NPM packages enforcing consistency and patterns across the organization. Drive team collaboration through architectural governance, review processes, and cross-functional alignment.
  • Drive Developer Platform Strategy: Create developer tools and automation that streamline workflows and boost productivity across engineering teams. Build repeatable AI-assisted workflows for frontend implementation, browser testing, debugging, framework migrations, and delivery—from a task specification to a validated pull request. Author technical documentation and mentor engineers through code reviews.
  • Enable Reliable Coding Agent Workflows: Structure repositories, component libraries, documentation, and development environments so engineers and coding agents can reliably build, test, and extend the platform. Establish clear component contracts, runnable examples, predictable build and test commands, and reusable skills and integrations that provide relevant company context and actionable validation feedback.
  • Establish Shared Patterns for AI-Powered Experiences: Partner with product and AI platform teams to establish shared UI patterns for AI-powered experiences, including streaming responses, progress visibility, cancellation, error recovery, and user approval of consequential actions. Design reusable components with clear contracts that reduce integration time across teams.
  • Strengthen Testing and Validation: Establish fast, reliable feedback through component tests, browser automation, visual regression checks, and CI gates so changes can be validated consistently across teams. Define validation and human review requirements for AI-generated changes.
  • Drive Adoption and Measurable Outcomes: Pilot new workflows with engineering teams, measure delivery time, escaped defects, reliability, and AI usage cost, and turn successful approaches into supported company standards. Verify that tools, integrations, and workflows operate successfully in the teams and environments where they are adopted.
  • Partner on Secure AI-Assisted Development: Work with Security and the AI platform team to establish scoped tool access, safe handling of secrets and sensitive data, and clear accountability for agent-generated changes. Define appropriate human review and approval boundaries for frontend workflows.
  • Drive Reliability & Performance: Lead optimization initiatives to reduce bundle size and costs. Spearhead framework migrations delivering critical security fixes. Implement performance monitoring and optimization strategies that reduce latency and improve load times.

What We're Looking For

  • At least 8 years of experience in frontend software development
  • At least 3 years of experience in frontend architecture with demonstrated organization-wide impact
  • Deep expertise with React and TypeScript; experience with Angular is highly valued
  • Experience with micro-frontend architectures (Module Federation, single-spa, Web Components, or similar approaches)
  • Strong knowledge of build tooling (Webpack, Vite, Rollup) and monorepo management
  • Experience with testing strategies (unit, integration, E2E) and establishing testing standards across teams, including component testing, browser automation, visual regression checks, and CI validation
  • Hands-on experience using AI coding tools to deliver production changes, with the ability to evaluate generated code, design effective validation, and explain where human review is necessary
  • Ability to demonstrate improvements in engineering delivery, quality, or reliability from AI-assisted workflows and drive adoption across teams
  • Practical understanding of scoped tool access, secrets, sensitive data, and accountability for AI-generated changes, in partnership with Security and AI platform teams
  • Excellent Communication: Strong verbal and written communication skills to effectively collaborate with team members and drive consensus across multiple teams.
  • Nice to have: Experience with observability platforms, CDN optimization, Next.js or other meta-frameworks, CI/CD pipelines, and AWS

The posted pay range represents the anticipated low and high end of the compensation for this position and is subject to change based on business need. To determine a successful candidate’s starting pay, we carefully consider a variety of factors, including primary work location, an evaluation of the candidate’s skills and experience, market demands, and internal parity.

For roles with on-target-earnings (OTE), the pay range includes both base salary and target incentive compensation. Target incentive compensation for some roles may include a ramping draw period. Compensation is higher for those who exceed targets. Candidates may receive more information from the recruiter.

About Supabase

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

About the Role

Supabase Storage is a scalable and high performance object storage service and is one of our fastest growing services. The current landscape of tools for uploading, storing, processing and delivering assets is complicated. Developers are forced to think about regions, caching, codecs and security before they can start uploading anything.

We are looking for engineers to solve this problem once and for all!

You will be working across the entire stack - client libraries, CLI, CDN, the storage server and the deployment infrastructure. One day, you might focus on improving upload resilience in iOS applications; the next, you could be optimizing the S3 protocol for efficient retries or finding ways to accelerate upload processing.

You will be contributing to both our open source server and upstream dependencies we use, like the TUS server.

This role is ideal for someone who thrives in async, fast-paced environments and is excited about building developer tools that scale to millions.

What You’ll Be Responsible For

  • Improving our analytics bucket offering and improving the storage of open file formats like iceberg and ducklake

  • Asset optimization to speed up delivery for websites and mobile applications

  • Building out our edge network to speed up uploads and build features like automatic cache invalidation

  • Improve the performance, observability, and reliability of our storage server

  • Work with the frontend team to build a fast, powerful storage explorer

  • Improve our APIs, client libraries and CLI to provide an exceptional end-to-end DX for our users

  • Resolve escalated support issues, while also identifying and resolving systemic issues across the platform

You Might Be a Good Fit If You

  • Have 5+ years backend engineering experience of running Node.js in production

  • Have experience with highly scalable, distributed systems

  • Are comfortable with working across the stack - backend application development, some infrastructure work including deploying, monitoring and scaling the service

  • Posses familiarity with observability tools (OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Grafana) and performance tuning

  • Have experience with production-grade PostgreSQL usage, including tuning and troubleshooting

  • Demonstrate an ownership mentality: driving projects end-to-end

  • Display empathy towards developer experience

Nice-to-have

  • Prior experience working on developer tools

  • Solid knowledge of cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP or Azure) and containerization (Docker, Kubernetes)

  • Direct experience designing and operating large file upload/download pipelines at scale

  • Deep, practical CDN integration and optimization knowledge

  • Experience with image and video processing tools (sharp, dssim, ffmpeg), formats and codecs (AVIF, WebM, Brotli) is a plus

  • Experience with the frontend ecosystem (Next.js, React, etc) is a plus

What We Offer

  • Fully Remote

    We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

  • ESOP

    Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

  • Tech Allowance

    Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

  • Health Benefits

Headquarters: Remote, USA

Help empower our global customers to connect to culture through their passions.

Why you’ll love this role:

StockX is the world’s leading marketplace for current culture, built at the intersection of commerce, community, and credibility. Trading Cards are foundational to StockX — not just as products, but as artifacts of fandom, nostalgia, speculation, and identity.

We are expanding how Trading Cards culture shows up on StockX through creator-driven, community-oriented commerce experiences that blend storytelling, expertise, and transaction. To do this well, we need category leaders who don’t just understand collectibles — they live inside them.

The Trading Cards Category Manager is the single-threaded owner of collectibles category growth within a new, high-priority commerce initiative. This person is the in-house expert on trading cards and sports cards, — and is responsible for translating that expertise into supply growth, engagement, and GMV.

You will act as:

  • The internal authority on the first-hand and second-hand trading cards ecosystem
  • The external face of StockX to collectors, breakers, shops, graders, dealers, and community leaders
  • The architect of the trading cards go-to-market playbook for this new initiative

This role blends deep cultural fluency, strategic ownership, and hands-on execution. Early on, you will own everything related to trading cards within this initiative. As the category scales, you will grow into a leader overseeing a broader trading cards portfolio and team.

What You’ll Do:

Own the Collectibles Category End-to-End

  • Define and execute the growth strategy for trading cards within the platform
  • Own category-level performance across supply, engagement, and revenue
  • Establish quarterly goals, leading indicators, and operating rhythms

Be the Market & Culture Expert

Maintain deep, current knowledge of trading card culture, including:

  • Key sellers, breakers, dealers, shops, graders, creators, and brands
  • Sub-segments such as trading cards (sports and TCG), graded sports cards, etc.
  • Product drops, set releases, grading cycles, convention moments, and cultural spikes
  • Pricing dynamics, liquidity, population reports, grading premiums, and resale economics

Serve as the internal voice of the trading cards community, informing product, marketing, and platform decisions.

Supply & Creator Acquisition

  • Build and own a pipeline of high-impact sellers across trading cards, sports cards, etc.
  • Personally recruit and onboard flagship sellers, breakers, comic shops, etc. who set the tone for the platform
  • Develop seller strategies that balance credibility, storytelling, and commerce

Commerce Strategy & Category Moments

  • Identify and orchestrate trading card-specific moments, campaigns, and formats that drive engagement and conversion (e.g., major set releases, championship spikes, grading returns, convention cycles)
  • Partner with Category Marketing to design culturally authentic activations
  • Experiment with new approaches (live breaks, expert drops, themed auctions, etc.) and iterate quickly based on performance and feedback

Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Work closely with Account and Partnerships Managers to scale seller acquisition and support
  • Collaborate with Product and Engineering to shape features and tools that matter to collectors (e.g., condition transparency, grading integrations, pricing insights, population data visibility)
  • Provide clear, actionable insights from the market to influence roadmap prioritization

Build the Playbook

  • Document learnings, frameworks, and best practices that can be reused across future categories
  • Help define what “great” looks like for category ownership at StockX
  • Support hiring and onboarding as the trading card category team grows

About You:

  • Deeply embedded in trading card culture — you know the people, platforms, trends, grading standards, and economics, and you’re already plugged into the ecosystem
  • 5+ years of experience in category management, partnerships, marketplace growth, brand, dealer, or operator roles within trading cards, sports cards, comics, toys, coins, or adjacent enthusiast ecosystems
  • Comfortable owning outcomes, not just strategy — you execute, iterate, and adapt
  • Strong relationship builder with credibility among collectors, breakers, shop owners, graders, dealers, and community members
  • Data-literate and commercially minded — you understand pricing spreads, grading premiums, liquidity, margin structures, and incentives
  • Entrepreneurial, scrappy, and energized by building something from the ground up

Nice to Have:

  • Existing network of card breakers, LCS owners, comic shops, grading submitters, toy dealers, or coin specialists
  • Experience buying, selling, grading, or operating within collectibles marketplaces
  • Familiarity with grading ecosystems (e.g., card and comic grading workflows, condition standards, population reports)
  • Experience with content-driven commerce, live selling, or enthusiast communities
  • Experience working cross-functionally with product and engineering teams
  • Experience running your own collectibles business, shop, or online storefront

Why This Role Matters:

Trading Cards will define the early perception and success of this new commerce initiative at StockX. This role sets:

  • The cultural and credibility bar for the platform
  • The go-to-market blueprint for future enthusiast categories
  • StockX’s reputation within trading cards

You will have outsized influence on how StockX expands its leadership from marketplace into deeper cultural engagement within the global trading card ecosystem.

StockX is proud to be a Detroit-based technology leader focused on the large and growing online market for sneakers, apparel, accessories, electronics, collectibles, trading cards, and more. data.title: Lead Product Management
data.description:
Headquarters: Remote

About Carrot:

Carrot is the leading global fertility and family care platform, built on intelligent care orchestration: the right clinical guidance, at the right moment, in the context of each member’s life. More than a thousand multinational employers, health plans, and health systems trust Carrot to support millions of members across 195 countries – from pre-pregnancy through menopause and major life moments in between. Carrot's comprehensive clinical program delivers industry-leading cost savings for plan sponsors and award-winning experiences and improved outcomes for millions of people worldwide.

Carrot is widely regarded as a defining force in healthcare innovation as a recipient of several top-tier awards, including Fast Company's 'Most Innovative Companies' and CNBC's '100 Barrier Breaking Startups'. The company is regularly cited by leading global outlets — including The Economist, Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, NPR, ABC News, and Harvard Business Review — as a leading voice on digital health, the future of work, and family health. Learn more at get-carrot.com.

The Opportunity

Carrot is seeking a Lead, Product Management to help shape and scale one of our core product areas as Carrot's platform continues to grow. In this role, you'll operate as a strategic driver within the Product organization — owning a significant portion of the product roadmap, setting direction for cross-functional initiatives, and raising the bar for product craft across the team.

This is a highly visible, high-impact role for someone who has already demonstrated strong product judgment and is ready to take on greater scope: shaping strategy, mentoring other product managers, and partnering directly with senior leadership on the initiatives that matter most to our members and business.

If you're energized by solving ambiguous, high-stakes problems and want to help define how Carrot builds products at scale, this role is for you!

What You’ll Own

In this role, you will:

  • Own the end-to-end product strategy and roadmap for a key product area, translating company priorities into a clear, prioritized plan of execution
  • Lead cross-functional initiatives, aligning Engineering, UX, Clinical, Legal, and Commercial partners around a shared vision and set of goals
  • Serve as a thought partner and informal mentor to other Product Managers, helping raise the bar on product process, discovery, and craft across the team
  • Make and communicate high-judgment prioritization decisions, balancing member experience, business impact, and technical feasibility
  • Partner directly with senior product and cross-functional leadership to shape quarterly and annual product strategy
  • Identify and address systemic gaps in process, tooling, or team practices that limit the Product team's effectiveness
  • Represent the Product team in executive and cross-functional forums, clearly communicating strategy, trade-offs, and outcomes

What Success Looks Like  

In your first 12–18 months, you will have:

  • Delivered a body of work that measurably improved member outcomes, engagement, or business performance within your product area
  • Built trusted, effective working relationships with cross-functional leaders across Engineering, UX, Clinical, Legal, and Commercial/Customer Success
  • Established yourself as a go-to product thought leader, with other PMs seeking out your input on strategy and process
  • Shaped or improved a core product process (discovery, roadmapping, prioritization) that is now used more broadly across the team
  • Successfully led at least one significant, ambiguous, cross-functional initiative from concept through launch

About You 

You likely have:

  • 5+ years of product management experience, including time at a fast-growing technology company; healthcare or digital health experience is a plus
  • A track record of owning complex, cross-functional product initiatives from strategy through execution
  • Strong product sense and the ability to balance user needs, business goals, and technical constraints in your decision-making
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence and align both peers and senior leadership
  • Experience mentoring or informally guiding less-experienced product managers

Nice to Have ⭐

While not required, we would be especially excited if you bring:

  • Experience in fertility, family-building, or broader digital health benefits
  • Experience partnering with Clinical or Legal teams on regulated or compliance-sensitive products
  • Familiarity with AI-enabled product features or workflows
  • Experience operating in a fully distributed, remote-first organization

Why This Role Matters 

As Carrot continues to scale, our Product team needs leaders who can operate with both strategic clarity and hands-on execution. This Lead, Product Management role is central to that effort — helping ensure our roadmap reflects the right priorities, our cross-functional partners are aligned, and our product practices scale sustainably as the team grows.

This is an opportunity to have an outsized impact: shaping not just a single product area, but the way Carrot's Product organization operates as it matures.

Interview Process 

We believe in a thoughtful and transparent interview process designed to create alignment for both candidates and our team.

For this role, candidates can expect:

  1. Recruiter Screen — 30 minutes
  2. Hiring Manager Interview — 30–45 minutes
  3. Cross-Functional Panel Interviews — 45 minutes
  4. Executive Leadership Conversation — 30 minutes
  5. Hiring Manager Wrap-Up — 15 minutes

Throughout the process, we will share additional context about the team, business priorities, customer landscape, and what success looks like in this role.

Why Candidates Join Carrot

Carrot offers the opportunity to do meaningful work in service of a deeply human mission.

Highlights include:

  • A mission-driven company focused on expanding access to fertility and family-forming care globally.
  • A high-growth environment where leaders are empowered to shape strategy and drive impact.
  • Competitive compensation, equity, and comprehensive benefits.
  • Flexible Time Off and a culture that actively encourages employees to recharge.
  • Comprehensive parental leave and family-forming benefits.
  • A collaborative, inclusive, and values-driven culture.
  • The opportunity to work alongside passionate, thoughtful teammates committed to improving healthcare outcomes worldwide.

Compensation: 

Carrot offers a holistic Total Rewards package designed to support our employees in all aspects of their life inside and outside of work, including health and wellness benefits, retirement savings plans, short- and long-term incentives, parental leave, family-forming assistance, and a competitive compensation package. The starting base salary for this position will range from $168,000-$198,000. Actual compensation may vary from posted base salary depending on your confirmed job-related skills and experience. 

Fraud and Security Notice: Please note that all communication regarding job opportunities at Carrot will come exclusively from an @get-carrot.com email address. If you receive messages from any other domain, please disregard them and report the incident to: securityreporting@get-carrot.com

A Note on AI

At Carrot, we believe AI can help us work smarter, move faster, and create more meaningful experiences for our members, customers, and each other. While not every role requires deep technical AI expertise, we value people who are curious, eager to learn, and excited to thoughtfully incorporate AI into their day-to-day work.

For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement—and we'll call that out clearly in the qualifications. For everyone else, we're looking for people who embrace new ways of working, use AI responsibly to improve quality and efficiency, and continue to learn as the technology evolves.

Why Carrot?

Carrot has received national and international recognition for its pioneering work, including Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies and World Changing Ideas, Inc. Power Partners, and Modern Healthcare’s Innovators. Carrot’s global workforce has been acknowledged with several accolades, including Fortune’s Best Workplaces in Healthcare, Great Place to Work, and Age-Friendly Employer certifications. Carrot is regularly featured in media reporting on issues related to the future of work, women in leadership, and healthcare innovation, including MSNBC, The Economist, Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, CNBC, National Public Radio, Harvard Business Review, and more. Learn more at carrotfertility.com.

data.description:
OnTrac is hiring a Senior Enterprise Architect!

Are you eager to join a dynamic and expanding company where you can both learn and make a meaningful impact? If you possess a strong sense of empathy, enjoy assisting others, thrive in a fast-paced environment, and excel at problem-solving, we encourage you to apply today to connect with a recruiter!

Founded in 1986, OnTrac has evolved into the leading provider of same-day and next-day delivery services in the U.S. for premier e-commerce and product-supply businesses, including five of the largest retailers in the U.S.

Location:

REMOTE: This position may be performed remotely in states where the company is authorized to employ individuals.

Compensation:

The expected starting base pay range for this position is $180,000 - $225,000, with full potential base salary range over a successful candidate’s tenure in the position of $180,000 - $270,000. Actual compensation will be determined based on experience, skills, internal equity, and other job-related factors. This position may also be eligible for bonus, commission, or other incentive compensation in accordance with the terms of the applicable plan of up to a 25% Bonus Target.

Employment Logistics:

Reporting to the CTO, this position is a hands-on, highly technical architect responsible for designing and building the AI-native platform, data, and integration architecture that powers OnTrac’s last mile delivery network. Working across platform, core, and domain engineering teams, this position defines the target-state architecture on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) for generative AI, agentic workflows, and real-time data, proves designs through proofs of concept and reference implementations, and partners with engineers to take them into production. The role brings deep expertise in LLM frameworks, Model Context Protocol (MCP), multi-agent systems, data engineering, API management, architecture patterns, and DevOps and LLMOps, and keeps the organization at the forefront of rapidly evolving AI technology.

Unpacking the Benefits:

Employees are eligible for a comprehensive benefits package which may include:

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Life and short- and long-term disability coverage
  • 401(k) retirement savings plan with company match
  • Flex vacation in states other than CA, CO, IL, MA, MT, and NE, with accruals up to 96 hours for first year of employment with tenure-based increases up to 160 hours
  • Two (2) floating holidays per year
  • Paid sick leave*
  • Six (6) paid company holidays
  • Two (2) weeks paid pregnancy disability leave, four (4) weeks paid parental bonding leave
  • Additional wellness and employee assistance programs

Benefits eligibility and offerings are subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable plans and company policies.

The Must-Haves:

This position requires a Bachelor’s degree or equivalent and 10 years of relevant experience in software engineering, data engineering, or solution architecture, including at least 7 years in an architecture role and 2 years of hands-on generative AI or LLM solution delivery. MUST HAVE 3 years of hands-on experience designing, building, and running production solutions on Google Cloud Platform (GCP). MUST HAVE 3 years of experience in the last mile delivery, parcel, or logistics industry, supporting technology for delivery operations such as route planning, sortation, scanning, tracking, or driver and dispatch systems. MUST HAVE experience designing and implementing enterprise API management and integration platforms, such as Apigee, MuleSoft, Kong, or Azure API Management.

Success in this role requires:

  • Deep, hands-on knowledge of agentic AI, including agent frameworks (such as Google ADK, LangGraph, or CrewAI), multi-agent orchestration, tool and function calling, agent memory, Model Context Protocol (MCP), and agent-to-agent (A2A) protocols.
  • Expert knowledge of GCP architecture and its AI and data services, such as Vertex AI, Gemini, Vertex AI Vector Search, BigQuery, Dataflow, Pub/Sub, GKE, Cloud Run, and Apigee.
  • Expert knowledge of data engineering for AI, including data modeling, batch and stream processing, ETL/ELT, change data capture (CDC), lakehouse design, feature and vector stores, data quality, and data governance.
  • Strong knowledge of API management and integration, including API design standards, gateways, OAuth 2.0 and OIDC, event streaming with Kafka and Pub/Sub, and exposing APIs as tools for AI agents.
  • Strong DevOps, MLOps, and LLMOps skills, including Terraform, CI/CD tooling (such as GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, or Cloud Build), Kubernetes, model and prompt versioning, automated evaluation, and LLM observability tools.
  • Understanding of last mile delivery and parcel logistics, including the parcel lifecycle, scan events, network planning, routing, geospatial data, and driver and carrier operations, and where AI creates value in each.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced environment, balance hands-on engineering with architectural leadership, and prioritize multiple initiatives.

Google Cloud Professional certifications, such as Professional Cloud Architect, Professional Machine Learning Engineer, or Professional Data Engineer and experience establishing an AI center of excellence, agent platform, or reference architectures and standards in a product-led technology organization are strongly preferred.

Your Mission in Motion:

A summary of key responsibilities for the role is outlined below. Additional duties may be assigned as needed to support business objectives.

  • Define and own the target-state architecture for OnTrac’s AI-native logistics platform on GCP, spanning shared platform services, reusable core services, domain applications, and the AI and agent layer that runs across them.
  • Design and build agentic and multi-agent systems, including agent orchestration, planning and tool use, memory and state management, human-in-the-loop controls, and agent-to-agent (A2A) communication.
  • Architect the MCP server ecosystem that exposes core logistics services (orders, shipments, tracking, locations, routing) and enterprise data as governed, reusable tools for internal and external AI agents.
  • Design AI-ready data platforms, including batch and real-time streaming pipelines, lakehouse and warehouse architectures, feature stores, and vector stores, using services such as BigQuery, Dataflow, Pub/Sub, Spanner, AlloyDB, and Vertex AI Vector Search.
  • Define a canonical, unified data model and event taxonomy for orders, shipments, scan events, locations, containers, and drivers, published as versioned contracts and as semantic context for LLMs and agents, with data quality, lineage, and governance built in.
  • Define the API and integration architecture, including API-first design, REST, gRPC, and asynchronous APIs, OpenAPI and AsyncAPI contracts, API management through Apigee, and event-driven integration over Pub/Sub and Kafka, serving applications and AI agents alike.
  • Apply and document architecture patterns for distributed and AI systems, including microservices, domain-driven design, event sourcing, CQRS, and saga, alongside agentic patterns such as ReAct, planner-executor, supervisor and router agents, and advanced RAG, and publish reference architectures for engineering teams.
  • Build proofs of concept, prototypes, and reference implementations hands-on to validate new models, agent frameworks, and AI tools, de-risk designs, and move quickly from experiment to production; write production-quality code alongside engineering teams.
  • Apply AI to last mile delivery capabilities, including intelligent order intake, address validation and geocoding, route optimization, delivery promise and ETA prediction, exception management, AI-powered control tower operations, driver and dispatch assistance, and conversational customer experiences.
  • Lead architecture and design reviews, author architecture decision records (ADRs), contribute to architecture governance and AI technology selection, and mentor engineers across teams.

Paving your way to your success:

  • You are a hands-on, highly technical architect responsible for designing and building the AI-native platform, data, and integration architecture that powers OnTrac’s last mile delivery network.
  • You work across platform, core, and domain engineering teams, defining the target-state architecture on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) for generative AI, agentic workflows, and real-time data, proving designs through proofs of concept and reference implementations, and partner with engineers to take them into production.
  • You bring deep expertise in LLM frameworks, Model Context Protocol (MCP), multi-agent systems, data engineering, API management, architecture patterns, and DevOps and LLMOps, and keep the organization at the forefront of rapidly evolving AI technology.

  • The salary range above represents the national range for this position. The salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at OnTrac, and the actual base offered may vary depending on several factors including, but not limited to: geographic location, candidate experience and qualifications, job-related skills and competencies, market alignment, and financial considerations.

data.title: Platform Engineer - Compute Capacity
data.description:
About Supabase

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

About the Role

We are seeking a platform engineer to join our Compute Capacity team. This team owns the capacity plan that keeps compute supply ahead of demand across every region we operate in — the forecasting, buffer policy, and provisioning systems that make sure a project never runs into a wall it didn't know was there.

You'll work on the systems that turn a capacity plan into provisioned reality: reservation acquisition, fleet reconciliation, and the automation that keeps what we've committed to in sync with what we're actually running. You'll help build the metrics and alerting that let capacity problems surface months out, on vendor lead time, rather than at the moment someone needs the room.

You'll design, build, and operate systems that are both robust and highly automated — helping us hold the right buffer at the right cost, catch drift before it becomes a shortage, and give every team a single, trustworthy view of how much room we have across the millions of databases we manage.

What You'll Be Responsible For

  • Help build and maintain the capacity plan that keeps Supabase's compute supply ahead of demand across regions and instance families

  • Support buffer policy by modeling headroom targets and their cost tradeoffs for review and sign-off

  • Build and maintain automation that turns the capacity plan into provisioned reality — reservation acquisition and top-up, fleet reconciliation, drift detection between committed and running capacity

  • Extend our infrastructure as code for capacity-relevant provisioning

  • Instrument capacity: build and maintain metrics for saturation, reservation coverage, idle buffer, forecast error, and provisioning latency

  • Build and tune capacity alerting so headroom, quota, and reservation issues surface months out rather than at the moment of impact

  • Support the demand gate — helping intake large customer commitments, launches, migrations, and new regions so they reach the plan before they reach the fleet

  • Contribute to mitigation projects: right-sizing, instance-family migrations, autoscaling improvements, workload consolidation

  • Help drive down compute cost per database through right-sizing, placement, and commitment coverage work

  • Participate in capacity incident response and post-incident follow-through

You Might Be A Good Fit If You

  • Have 5+ years across infrastructure engineering, SRE, platform, or capacity engineering, ideally at SaaS or cloud infrastructure scale

  • Have production software engineering experience — you've owned and operated a service, not just a notebook. Comfortable in modern languages like TypeScript, Python, and Go

  • Are comfortable working against forecasts and assumptions that are incomplete, and can revise your work as those assumptions change

  • Have experience with Infrastructure as Code (Pulumi or Terraform)

  • Have built or maintained observability for systems you own — metrics that answer real questions and alerting people trust (Prometheus/Grafana, CloudWatch, or similar);

  • Have solid working knowledge of AWS EC2: instance families and generations, purchase options, capacity reservations, and quota mechanics

  • Have some financial fluency — you understand reservation economics and the basic tradeoffs between coverage, utilization, and cost

  • Communicate clearly across audiences, from engineers to finance stakeholders

What We Offer

  • Fully Remote

    We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

  • ESOP

    Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

  • Tech Allowance

    Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

  • Health Benefits

    Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

  • Annual Off-Sites

    Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

  • Flexible Work

    We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

  • Professional Development

    Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

About the Team

Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

  • ~400 team members

  • 60+ countries

  • 20+ languages spoken

  • Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)

  • 540,000+ community members

We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

Moodle with us!

At Moodle, we’re on a mission to empower educators and learners worldwide with open, flexible, and innovative digital learning solutions. As the world’s most customizable and trusted open-source LMS, we partner with schools, universities, and organizations to create better learning experiences for millions. If you’re ready to make a real impact, and be part of a global movement shaping the future of learning, join us. Let's transform education together!

About the Role

Join our team as the Senior Manager, DevOps and become a key leader in delivering cutting-edge technology for our external customers, vendors, and clients. You will manage a fully remote high-performing team dedicated to maintaining and optimizing our critical infrastructure, ensuring peak performance and security. This includes overseeing stability and performance tuning, customer upgrades and migrations, and implementing robust security measures. You will be instrumental in managing the customer support requests and guaranteeing seamless, 24-hour monitoring and support. This is an exciting opportunity to expand the business and make a significant impact on our technology delivery.

Senior Manager, DevOps - Drive Innovation and Infrastructure Excellence (US)

Managing the delivery of technology for external customers, vendors, and other clients to improve and expand the business, the Senior Manager, DevOps is responsible for managing the team maintaining our infrastructure to perform optimally including: maintaining stability of systems, proactive monitoring, servicing customer support requests, removal of technical debt, and being part of a team that pushes our infrastructure forward.

This role will support important security certification projects and work within federal client boundaries. Successful applicants must be US citizens with willingness and ability to receive necessary security clearances.

What You’ll Do

Most days in this role usually involve a mix of:

  • Support DevOps team in managing client hosting infrastructure
  • Lead the team in best practices for deployment, availability, performance and automation
  • Manage and participate in the on-call rotation as needed
  • Provide technical expertise, recommendations and evaluations to the management team
  • Assist with coordinating tasks that need to be completed as part of certification processes and procedures as required (SOC2, FedRamp, ISO, etc.)
  • Assist in the development and implementation of department wide operational policies including security, process, and support policies
  • Assist Sales with scoping and pricing non-standard implementations and infrastructure requests
  • Manage the DevOps team to ensure the availability and reliability of the Moodle Services hosting platforms
  • Coach and mentor DevOps team members
  • Manage and prioritize team workloads, including managing incoming support and infrastructure requests
  • Represent the DevOps team in customer facing meetings where required
  • Review priorities and with the Global Head of Infrastructure to align work with strategic priorities
  • Represent the DevOps team to the wide company
  • Be responsible for the career development and performance of direct reports

We’d love to meet you

Especially if you can tell us about your:

  • Extensive experience as a technical lead or manager leading complex, distributed, and remote teams, particularly in large scale environments
  • Strong customer facing skills
  • Working experience using modern team management methodologies. Agile, SCRUM, are preferred
  • Knowledge of best practices related to high availability, fault tolerance, performance and disaster recovery
  • 5 years of Linux/Unix system administration experience and AWS hosted infrastructure
  • Knowledge of Python, PHP, shell scripting or other scripting languages an advantage
  • Extensive experience troubleshooting network, system and application issues
  • Amazing problem solving, analysis and communication skills
  • Being available for on-call support and occasional out of hours work
  • US citizenship with willingness and ability to obtain appropriate security clearances for US government projects.

Experience in the following areas is a plus:

  • Configuring and supporting monitoring tools such as Prometheus, Grafana, NewRelic.

What's in it for you?

Moodle has a globally diverse team with over 280 team members in more than 25 countries around the world. We’ve built a passionate team of hard-working, driven and diverse people from all over the world, united by a shared belief in the ability of our platform to make a positive difference to our world. Learn more about Moodle

Moodle is the world’s most trusted online learning solution, with a growing ecosystem of products and services, including Moodle Workplace, Moodle App, MoodleCloud, and more. The engine of our ecosystem is Moodle LMS, the secure and customizable open source learning management platform used by well over 300 million learners worldwide.

Find out more about us on our website.

data.description:
Location:Remote

Job Type:Full-time

About Us!

At Ready Computing, we specialize in data-centric IT solutions that help organizations across healthcare, supply chain, finance, and manufacturing optimize their technology and data strategies. With offices in the U.S. and the UK, we provide expert consulting, development, and managed services to clients worldwide. We're committed to hiring top talent to drive innovation, particularly in the healthcare IT space.

The Software Architect designs Wellbase, Ready Computing’s managed services suite for healthcare and social-care organizations, and remains hands-on through implementation. Wellbase provides hosting, monitoring, analytics, and security to keep mission-critical systems available, secure, and improving. This player-coach role involves designing and owning end-to-end solutions while leading a small delivery team.

The work includes Wellbase’s agentic AI companion (Lucas), governed and auditable Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations, policy and governance services, and product demonstration and staging environments. The role calls for curiosity about emerging technologies, confidence presenting architecture and tradeoffs to executives, and a strong sense of ownership.

What you'll do

Essential duties and responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following:

  • Define technical requirements and target architecture for new platform capabilities, and stay accountable through design, implementation, and release.
  • Design and lead delivery of agentic AI solutions, including tool-using agents, evaluation approaches, and safe integration with healthcare workflows.
  • Architect and extend MCP-based services that connect agents and applications to enterprise systems, data, and licensed capabilities.
  • Own architecture for policy and governance services that control access, content decisions, and regulated use of data and AI.
  • Shape the architecture of demo and staging environments so new capabilities can be shown reliably to customers and executives.
  • Lead a small team as a player-coach: set technical direction, review design and code, and implement the hardest pieces yourself.
  • Present architecture, options, and recommendations to executive stakeholders; take ownership of decisions and outcomes.
  • Apply CI/CD, cloud, and Kubernetes deployment practices to keep the platform releasable and operable.
  • Mentor developers and raise the quality bar for design, security, and delivery.
  • Produce and maintain technical documentation that others can build from.
  • Design and optimize data stores (relational and, where needed, vector or other specialized stores) to support agents, applications, and governance.
  • Implement authorization, policy, and security controls appropriate to healthcare and other regulated data.
  • Perform other duties and special projects as assigned.

What you bring

Technical Skills

  • Expertise in software architecture and design patterns for cloud-native and service-based enterprise systems.
  • Strong proficiency in Python and/or Java, with the ability to work across a polyglot stack.
  • Hands-on experience with cloud platforms (Google Cloud preferred), containers, Docker, and Kubernetes.
  • Experience designing REST APIs and distributed services; familiarity with workflow or orchestration systems is a plus.
  • Experience with CI/CD pipelines and development tools such as Git, Jenkins, and JIRA.
  • Database design and optimization, primarily relational (PostgreSQL); exposure to vector or search stores is a plus.
  • Familiarity with enterprise frameworks such as Spring or FastAPI.
  • Working knowledge of policy-as-code, authorization frameworks, or similar governance controls is a plus.
  • Some hands-on experience with agentic AI development (LLM-based agents, tool use or MCP, evaluation design, or similar).
  • Familiarity with observability and monitoring technologies such as Prometheus, Grafana, and OpenTelemetry (OTel).
  • Demonstrated curiosity and a track record of evaluating and adopting new technologies where they create real leverage.

Qualaifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Software Development, Computer Science, or a related field.
  • Minimum of 8 years of software development experience with a focus on enterprise-level architectures, including hands-on design and implementation. Some experience building or leading agentic AI solutions is required.
  • Comfort working with healthcare or other regulated data environments.
  • Deep healthcare-interoperability experience is helpful but not required.

Core Competencies

  • Technical Architectural Leadership: Architects scalable, future-ready solutions and leads a small team through implementation, remaining hands-on on the hardest work.
  • Solution Ownership: Takes end-to-end accountability for designs and outcomes, from first concept through delivery and operation.
  • Curiosity and Innovation: Actively explores new technologies and approaches, especially in agentic AI and platform engineering, and applies them with sound judgment.
  • Executive Communication: Presents architecture, options, and recommendations clearly to executive audiences, and translates complex technical concepts for diverse stakeholders.
  • Analytical Problem-Solving: Diagnoses and resolves intricate technical challenges in order to keep programs moving.
  • Attention to Detail & Security: Maintains rigorous standards in design and development to ensure the reliability, scalability, and security of enterprise solutions.

Physical & Mental Qualifications:

We're now expanding beyond communication into building the best possible learning experiences for kids everywhere.

We're a small, high-talent-density team with experience from leading technology companies. We value ownership, speed, and thoughtful decision-making, and we aim to create an environment where people can do the best work of their careers.

We're hiring an Engineering Leader to own ClassDojo's Platform engineering org end-to-end for infrastructure, data, developer experience, and AI tooling.

As the Engineering Lead for Platform, you'll manage the engineering managers across these teams as well as perform the EM role for teams when needed. You’ll work with our product engineering areas as your customers, set platform engineering practices and quality, and make the build-vs-buy and architecture trade-offs that shape how every engineer at ClassDojo ships.

This is a manager-of-managers role with real architectural and strategic ownership. You'll have 2 to 4 engineering managers reporting in, and your work multiplies across the entire engineering org. You will be expected to set direction, not just execute on it.

What You'll Do

Lead a multi-team Platform org

  • Own Platform's company-level objectives and the engineering plan that delivers them.

  • Translate company priorities and product-engineering needs into a platform roadmap, in a way that flows both up and down.

  • Be responsible for build-vs-buy and architecture-level trade-offs across infrastructure, data, developer experience, and AI tooling; own the technical roadmap and how it balances against the needs of your customers.

  • Represent Platform and collaborate with cross-functional leadership partners and in engineering-wide leadership conversations.

Develop the engineering managers reporting to you

  • Coach EMs to a higher bar with clear feedback, growth plans, and direct support.

  • Drive AI-native development in line with ClassDojo’s engineering practices (flow-based delivery, vertical slicing, WIP discipline, Definition of Done, observability)

  • Address performance issues early and clearly; develop managers out of "fine" performance into great performance.

  • Be directive when our values, quality bar, or ways of working are at stake.

Run platform towards the long term

  • Treat the product engineering areas as customers: understand their needs, measure adoption and satisfaction, and prioritize accordingly.

  • Build paved roads and golden paths that teams want to use; earn adoption rather than mandating it.

  • Take accountability for SLAs/SLOs and incident response across the platform surface.

  • Make tech-debt and reliability trade-offs on purpose, not by accident.

Drive technical excellence across the platform

  • Support and drive architecture and systems design decisions across infrastructure, data, DevEx, and AI tooling; ensure systems are reliable, maintainable, and operationally ready.

  • Make build-vs-buy calls deliberately; avoid both not-invented-here and unmanaged sprawl.

Partner cross-functionally

  • Partner with Security, Ops, Data, and other functions as the platform requires.

  • 2+ years managing managers, with direct reports who were themselves people managers.

About the Team

OpenAI, in close collaboration with our capital partners, is embarking on a journey to build the world’s most advanced AI infrastructure ecosystem. This role bridges the interface between data center construction and hardware landing, ensuring seamless integration of mission-critical infrastructure with hardware deployment timelines. You will define and execute commissioning plans, support infrastructure bring-up, and take ownership of operations and maintenance for cutting-edge, large-scale, AI data centers.

You will collaborate closely with design, construction, and hardware teams to define repeatable processes for new data center builds and lead hands-on operations to uphold the performance and reliability of our deployed infrastructure.

data.description:
Luxury Presence is building the AI growth platform for real estate. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and other top investors, we're a Series C company that has hit $100M in annual recurring revenue. More than 90,000 real estate professionals, including over 30% of the WSJ Real Trends top 100 agents in the United States, use us to run and grow their business.

The Opportunity

We're hiring a Senior DevOps Engineer to build the AI-native, self-service infrastructure platform that powers how Luxury Presence ships software. It's a platform where every developer, human or agent, can validate a change in minutes, understand failures immediately, and ship confidently.

You'll join a small, high-leverage Infrastructure team with a clear mandate: multiply what every engineer and agent can do through automation, self-service, and guardrails-by-design. The goal is a platform where self-service is the default and human intervention is the exception, and you'll help make that real.

What You'll Do

  • Build and operate the self-service infrastructure platform. Make the right thing the easy thing, and the secure thing the default.

  • Build the golden paths engineers and agents ship on. Within a technical direction set by the team's Staff engineers, build and operate the layers they rely on (a unified CI/CD pipeline, GitOps-based delivery with ArgoCD, an IaC module catalog, and scaffolding for new services), owning specific components end to end. The goal is for engineers and agents to provision infrastructure and ship changes within guardrails, without hand-writing Terraform/Kustomize or waiting on a ticket.

  • Make agents first-class developers. Help generalize our agent isolation pattern into reusable platform primitives: sandboxed runtime, workload identity, audit trails, and approval gates. Every agent action runs on the same identity, audit, ownership, cost-attribution, and approval rails as a human.

  • Build and operate the validation platform and quality gates. Provide the rails that teams validate changes on before production: ephemeral PR environments with auto-teardown, plus the security, performance, and load-testing gates developers rely on. Implement new gates as coverage grows, keep them fast and low-flake, and drive services onto them. Make gate and test results machine-readable and callable outside the PR flow, so agents and humans alike can act on a failure directly.

  • Own the reliability and observability of what you build. Create the dashboards and operational controls that make the surfaces you own observable and improvable as throughput grows: gate pass rates, approval-rate and self-service-ratio trends, common failure modes, cost attribution, and DORA metrics surfaced to teams. Carry on-call for those surfaces and run incidents from detection through follow-up, turning recurring toil into automation and runbooks other engineers reuse.

What We're Looking For

  • Senior-level experience in SRE, DevOps, or Platform Engineering. You've built and operated production infrastructure at scale and can own a significant workstream end to end with limited oversight.

  • Full incident-ownership experience: you've carried on-call for systems you built and driven incidents from detection through follow-up.

  • Excellent cross-team communication: you can translate platform constraints into developer-friendly solutions and documentation.

Bonus Points

  • Identity, access, and policy-as-code experience: workload/service identity (SPIFFE/SPIRE, OIDC), short-lived credentials, secrets management (Vault), and policy enforcement.

  • Experience building self-service developer platforms, ephemeral environments, CLIs, scaffolding tools, or internal developer portals (Backstage or custom). You treat infrastructure as a product.

Our Tech Stack

Lambda, The Superintelligence Cloud, is a leader in AI cloud infrastructure serving tens of thousands of customers. Our customers range from AI researchers to enterprises and hyperscalers. Lambda's mission is to make compute as ubiquitous as electricity and give everyone the power of superintelligence. One person, one GPU.

If you'd like to build the world's best AI cloud, join us.

*Note: This position requires presence in our San Francisco, San Jose, or Bellevue office location 4 days per week; Lambda’s designated work from home day is currently Tuesday.

The Role

Lambda’s Core Cloud Platform organization builds the software and services that turn large-scale GPU infrastructure into reliable, customer-facing cloud products. The team owns foundational platform capabilities across Managed Kubernetes, resource lifecycle, workload orchestration, cloud APIs, automation, observability, and multi-region operations.

The immediate focus for this role includes evolving Lambda’s Managed Kubernetes platform: making it easier and safer to provision, upgrade, operate, and scale Kubernetes clusters for demanding AI workloads. The platform integrates closely with Lambda’s underlying compute, networking, storage, fleet, and security systems.

As Engineering Manager, you will lead a team building and operating these foundational platform services. You will own the team’s people, execution, technical quality, and production outcomes while partnering with senior engineers to set technical direction. This is a high-leverage role at the intersection of cloud infrastructure, distributed systems, Kubernetes, and the customer experience.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead the design, implementation, and production operation of foundational cloud-platform services.

  • Own the technical roadmap for making the platform more distributed, resilient, observable, and operationally efficient.

  • Ensure the platform operates reliably across a growing multi-datacenter and multi-region fleet, including appropriate handling of partial failures and long-running workflows.

  • Partner with senior and staff engineers to make sound architectural decisions across distributed services, stateful systems, APIs, schedulers, controllers, and automation.

  • Define clear contracts and integration patterns between the cloud platform and the compute, networking, fleet, security, and customer-facing systems around it.

  • Lead and grow a team of senior and staff engineers; hire exceptionally, develop people, maintain a high-performance bar, and address underperformance directly.

  • Own project planning, prioritization, and delivery aligned with Lambda’s business objectives and customer commitments.

  • Establish strong engineering practices across design reviews, testing, CI/CD, observability, incident response, and on-call operations.

  • Collaborate with peer Engineering Managers and cross-functional partners to resolve dependencies and deliver complete customer outcomes.

  • Improve engineering leverage through automation, effective operating mechanisms, and responsible use of AI-assisted engineering.

  • Stay current with developments in Kubernetes, cloud-native infrastructure, GPU orchestration, and platform automation, and apply them where they materially improve Lambda’s platform.

You

  • 4+ years of engineering management experience with a demonstrated track record of growing high-performing teams

  • 7+ years of software engineering IC experience, including principal or staff-level ownership of mission-critical distributed systems

  • 8+ years implementing business-critical services in Python or Go, from conception through production

  • Experience building systems that coordinate across multiple independently-owned infrastructure services (compute, networking, storage) without owning them directly

  • Background in multi-region deployment strategies, cross-datacenter state management, and high-availability architectures

  • Strong track record of owning projects end-to-end: architecture, delivery, operations, and continuous improvement

  • Excellent cross-functional collaboration - proven ability to drive alignment across infrastructure, platform, and product teams

Nice to Have

  • Awareness of the evolving bare metal and GPU infrastructure ecosystem - including tools like NVIDIA NiCo (NCX Infra Controller) for DPU-enforced lifecycle automation, BlueField DPU capabilities, and where industry standards for multi-tenant bare metal management are heading

  • Experience evaluating or adopting vendor infrastructure tooling into an existing platform - performing a full migration, having the judgment to assess fit, risk, and timing

  • Familiarity with Kubernetes or Slurm - useful context for how this team integrates with Lambda’s cluster orchestration layer, but not required for the role itself

  • Experience in the AI, ML, or GPU hardware industry

  • Proven track record designing large-scale cloud IaaS platforms from the ground up

  • Exposure to IPO readiness, enterprise compliance, or security requirements at scale

Values We’re Looking For

  • Hands-on when needed: You can get into the details when the team or system needs it without becoming the long-term bottleneck.

  • High accountability: You take responsibility for delivery and production outcomes and do not tolerate systems remaining unreliable.

  • Business and customer alignment: You connect technical priorities to the outcomes that matter for Lambda and its customers.

  • Sound judgment: You make decisions with incomplete information, manage risk, and change direction when the evidence changes.

  • Systems builder: You create teams, processes, and technical foundations that operate effectively without depending on constant intervention.

  • Agency with context: You find responsible paths through obstacles without creating unnecessary risk or operating as a cowboy.

  • Low ego and strong collaboration: You handle disagreement directly, learn when you are wrong, and build productive cross-functional relationships.

  • Learning through failure: You turn operational and organizational failures into stronger systems and lasting improvements.

The annual salary range for this position has been set based on market data and other factors. However, a salary higher or lower than this range may be appropriate for a candidate whose qualifications differ meaningfully from those listed in the job description.

How will you make an impact?

  • We are seeking a highly skilled, technically authoritative and customer-facing Sr. Principal Hyperscale Rack Engineer within the Intelligent Infrastructure Segment to lead the architecture, integration, and strategic direction of advanced air and liquid-cooled server and network rack solutions for large-scale hyperscale deployments.

  • This role will serve as the senior technical authority responsible for translating customer requirements into scalable, manufacturable, and commercially viable rack systems.

  • As the Sr. Principal Hyperscale Rack Engineer, youwill operate at the intersection of engineering, customer engagement, and program execution – driving end-to-end rack architecture across mechanical, power, thermal, electrical, and software domains.

  • Success in this role requires deep technical expertise, strong commercial acumen, and the ability to lead complex programs while influencing both internal and external stakeholders.

What will you do?

  • Serve as the lead architect and development manager for complex rack-level solutions, owning system-level design decisions across mechanical, electrical, power, thermal, networking, and software integration domains.

  • Lead customer-facing technical engagements from RFI/RFQ all the way to first hardware delivery, including design reviews, trade-off discussions, and executive-level conversations.

  • Translate ambiguous or evolving customer requirements into clear program frameworks, ensuring alignment between customer expectations and engineering execution.

  • Demonstrate strong commercial awareness by effectively managing customer expectations, pushing back when requirements introduce risk or inefficiency, and confidently addressing challenging technical and cost-related questions.

  • Drive cross-functional alignment across all departments (executives, engineering, supply chain, manufacturing, and program) to ensure cohesive solution development with emphasis on Bill of Materials (BOM) management and scheduling.

  • Own rack-level architecture including power distribution design, thermal strategies (air and liquid cooling), cable routing, serviceability, and manufacturability.

  • Provide deep technical guidance on rack infrastructure including PDUs, busbars, liquid cooling systems (CDUs, manifolds, QDs), airflow design, and high-density compute integration.

  • Oversee architecture decisions impacting performance, cost, scalability, and deployment efficiency.

  • Drive program execution from concept through production, ensuring schedules are clearly defined, tracked, and met.

  • Apply strong program management discipline: define milestones, identify risks early, escalate issues proactively, and hold cross-functional teams accountable to commitments.

  • Drive readiness support calls internally from initial NPI scoping to prototyping to mass production, ensuring all systems are operable together from a power, thermal, and software standpoint.

  • Partner with customers and internal stakeholders to continuously refine designs based on deployment feedback and operational learnings.

  • Collaborate with compliance and certification teams to ensure mechanical designs meet global regulatory requirements (e.g., UL, CE, ISTA, ASTM).

  • Mentor and guide engineers across disciplines, establishing best practices in rack system architecture and integration.

  • Understanding of rack installation constraints, maintenance access, and serviceability in rack mechanical infrastructure.

  • Conduct root cause analysis and corrective actions for mechanical failures or field issues.

  • May perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

How will you get here?

Education:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or related field is required

Experience:

  • Minimum of 10 years’ experience in engineering, systems integration, or data center hardware design.

  • Minimum of 3 years’ rack-level (L11) solution design and integration experience.
